content: Kurnool Medical College, located in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, India, was established following the formation of Andhra State in October 1953. The government decided to set up a medical college in the Raayalaseema region, and on November 29, 1955, orders were issued to establish the institution. Initially, the college admitted 50 students in July 1956, even though the building was not yet ready. When Andhra Pradesh was formed and the capital moved to Hyderabad, the old secretariat building in Kurnool was handed over to the college. The institution was formally inaugurated on July 21, 1956, by Sri T.T. Krishnamachari, the then Finance Minister of India. The college initially offered non-clinical courses, with laboratories established for these subjects. By 1958, a clinical lecture hall and a clinical pathology laboratory were constructed, along with an air-conditioned mortuary capable of accommodating 24 bodies. On January 28, 1958, a new outpatient block at the Government General Hospital, Kurnool, which serves as the teaching hospital, was inaugurated by Sri D.K. Karmankar, the Health Minister of India. Clinical courses began at this time, and the first batch of second-year MBBS students joined the college. In July 1957, the first units in Medicine, Surgery, and Midwifery were established. The college was initially affiliated with Sri Venkateswara University in January 1957 and received permanent affiliation in January 1959. An NCC unit was started in January 1958, and laboratory technician and attender courses were introduced in October 1959. A Regional Laboratory was also established to serve the Raayalaseema districts. In 1961, an Animal House with separate units for different laboratory animals was built. A Central Workshop began operations in 1964. The men's hostel was initially located in the legislators' hostel in 1958, accommodating 175 students, with later expansions allowing for 350 students. The state guesthouse was converted into a women's hostel, and additional accommodations were provided in the hospital premises. A new extension, costing 2 crores, was nearly completed to house 150 more women students and 56 postgraduate women students. After vacating the sub-hostel for women, it was repurposed for postgraduate students, and new postgraduate quarters with 75 single rooms were constructed. In 1959, an Assembly-cum-Library Hall was built at a cost of Rs. 1,500,000. The Anatomy Department was expanded, and a clinical research block costing Rs. 600,000 was completed. A rural health center for teaching social and preventive medicine was opened in Parla village in 1960. The college offers a wide range of postgraduate degree and diploma courses, including MS (Anatomy), MD (Physiology), MD (Biochemistry), MD (Pharmacology), MD (Microbiology), MD (Pathology), and many others. Recently, the Medical Council of India inspected the college for recognition and the introduction of super-specialty courses such as DM (Neurology), DM (Gastroenterology), DM (Nephrology), MCh (Pediatric Surgery), MCh (Neurosurgery), MCh (Plastic Surgery), MCh (Cardiothoracic Surgery), DM (Cardiology), and MCh (Urology). In 2003, an Acute Medical Care (AMC) unit and an Intensive Coronary Care Unit (ICCU) were established at the Government General Hospital, Kurnool. Between 2001 and 2003, examination halls with a capacity of 400 each were constructed to accommodate the increased number of students. Renovations were carried out in the Physiology and Anatomy departments, and additional hostel accommodations were provided for both male and female students. Construction of a new mortuary building and a pathology laboratory was also undertaken. The college celebrated its Golden Jubilee in December 2006 and January 2007, marking 50 years since its establishment. Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, the then President of India, was invited to the celebrations. Kurnool Medical College has produced several notable alumni who have made significant contributions in various fields. Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu, a world-renowned radiation oncologist, pioneered the use of computerized brachytherapy treatment systems in the United States in 1979. He developed the transperineal brachytherapy technique, a non-surgical method for implanting radioactive seeds to treat cancer, significantly improving patients' quality of life. Dr. Nori, who serves as the Professor and Chairman of the Radiation Oncology Department at New York Presbyterian Hospital Weill-Cornell Medical Center, was honored with the Tribute to Life award by the American Cancer Society for his contributions to cancer research, treatment, and education. Dr. Sekhar Tam Tam was awarded the Member of the British Empire (MBE) in 2006 by Queen Elizabeth II for his service as District Medical Officer in Grenada. Other distinguished alumni include Dr. C.R.R.M. Reddy, Dr. Sita Devi, Dr. P.S.R.K. Haranath, Dr. D. Bhaskar Reddy, Dr. B. Sadasivudu, Dr. D. Nageshwara Reddy, Dr. P. Jagannath, Dr. W. Seetharam, Dr. Mukunda Reddy, Dr. Ramakrishna Reddy, Dr. Madhubala Reddy, and Dr. Babu Rao Mediyam, among others. The college has also produced prominent figures in politics, industry, and public service, such as Dr. S. Sailajanath (MLA), Dr. D.L. Ravindra Reddy (MLA), and Dr. S. Murali Krishna (IAS).
